stem: A company bought a computer for Rs 75,000. After 2 years the book value under the WDV method is Rs 48,000. What is the annual rate of depreciation (WDV rate) applied?

per_option_rationale.rationale: WDV: BV = Cost x (1-r)^n. So (1-r)^2 = 48000/75000 = 0.64. Taking square root: 1-r = 0.8. Therefore r = 0.20 = 20%.
Uses straight-line approach: total depreciation = 27000 over 2 years, so annual = 13500, rate = 13500/75000 = 18%; or assumes (1-r)^2 = 0.75 giving r = 25%.
Computes total depreciation 27000/75000 = 36% and divides by 2 to get 18%, using a linear-average approach on a geometric problem.
Computes (75000-48000)/75000 = 27000/75000 = 36% as if this is the single-year rate, ignoring that the 36% covers 2 compounding years.

explanation: Rearrange WDV formula: (1-r)^2 = BV/Cost = 48000/75000 = 0.64. Taking the positive square root: 1-r = sqrt(0.64) = 0.8. So r = 0.20, i.e. 20% per annum.

explanation_sections.punchline: Back-calculating the WDV rate requires taking the nth root of (BV/Cost) and subtracting from 1.
explanation_sections.approach: Formula: BV = C x (1-r)^n. Rearrange: (1-r)^n = BV/C = 48000/75000 = 0.64. Take nth root (n=2): 1-r = sqrt(0.64) = 0.8. r = 20%.
explanation_sections.lesson: To find the WDV rate from two data points, compute the ratio of book value to cost, take the appropriate root, then find r = 1 - root.
explanation_sections.timing: 65 seconds. Trap: dividing total percentage drop by number of years (linearising a geometric decay).
